title: Adaptive quantization profile loadbench and quality-sentry for FP16/INT8/INT4
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need an automated, repeatable harness that tests a curated set of quantization profiles (FP16 baseline, two INT8 variants, and at least one INT4 aggressive profile) across representative load shapes while measuring both performance (tokens/sec, p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate) and quality (embedding similarity, token-level edit distance on a labeled prompt set, and end-to-end functional checks). This ticket creates an adaptive loadbench and a quality-sentry that emits regression signals to CI and the Console ALERT pipeline. The harness should exercise model variants under steady-state, bursty, and long-conversation tail workloads and run nightly sweeps with regression detection and automated artifact uploads.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end nightly sweep over FP16, INT8-A, INT8-B, INT4 profiles and produces per-profile report in S3
Collected metrics include tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, KV-cache hit rate, memory peaks, and per-request token counts
Quality metrics computed for each profile: embedding cosine vs baseline, token-level edit distance on evaluation set, and top-1 generation drift (thresholds configurable)

Regression detection triggers when either latency p95 increases by >15% or quality metric falls below configured delta (e.g., embedding cosine < 0.985 or edit distance increase >4 tokens) and creates a CI alert with links to artifacts
Integration with Console: per-sweep dashboard tile and alert rule visible in Console > Regression Alerts
Playbook created with automatic fallback configuration (route to FP16 or INT8-safe variant) when regression is detected in production-like traffic
implementation_notes: Use existing load harness infra (load-agent-gpu pool) but add a new 'quant-profile' dimension to outputs
Bundle per-request context capture to compute embedding drift and to identify failure modes (e.g., hallucination patterns) later
Instrument runtime to emit KV-cache hit/miss tags; correlate cache hit rate with per-profile latency changes
Implement an adaptive schedule: start with low ramp, then steady-state, then synthetic bursts (2x, 5x, 10x) with background jitter to emulate multi-tenant traffic
Store raw traces and generated outputs in S3 with a stable prefix for automated diffing and auditability
Expose configuration as YAML in repo (quant_profiles.yaml) so product/infra can tweak test profiles without code change
test_plan: Create canonical evaluation prompt set (~120 prompts) covering chat, instruction, and long-context scenarios; store under drive: Quant-Perf-Eval-2025
Define quant profiles: fp16, int8-symmetric (safe), int8-asymmetric (aggressive), int4-hybrid (latency-focused)
Load shapes: steady 200 rps for 60 min, spike 1200 rps for 2 min repeated, long-tail stream with 1000 conversations maintaining KV cache state for 30 min
Run per-profile A/B deployments on a dedicated test pool to avoid impacting production traffic
Collect metrics via Prometheus/Grafana plus a consolidated CSV/JSON report with summary and raw traces
Run the sweep nightly; the CI job validates no regressions and posts a summary to #infra-quant on Slack
regression_detection: Regression engine compares current sweep to a chosen baseline (typically latest FP16 sweep). Calculation: normalized delta on p95 and quality metrics using bootstrap samples to avoid flukes. Alert thresholds are configurable per-model and per-profile. When triggered, a regression ticket is auto-created (ENG-REG-YYYY) with links to the failing traces and a suggested rollback to the last-good model/profile. The system should support suppression windows for known noisy tests and allow manual override via Console.
follow_ups: Hook CI gating: block merges if nightly sweep regression persists for >24h
Add user-facing guidance in docs: recommended quant profiles per workload type
Expand evaluation suite to include customer prompt samples for high-value customers (privacy-safe hashed inputs)
